# Neotoma — chronic vs. acute pain for the durable ICP (Candidate B)

## Subject

Splitting Candidate B's pain into the chronic tax they tolerate (re-prompting, cross-tool sync) versus the acute crisis that converts them (an agent acting confidently on wrong, stale, or lossy-compressed state), and marking which one should lead a product surface.

## Summary

The acute crisis — an agent acting confidently on wrong, stale, or lossy-compressed state, discovered downstream as a concrete loss — is the converting pain and must lead; the chronic re-prompting/sync/opacity/token-cost tax is real, corroborated, and tolerated, and must not lead (operator-ruled 2026-08-21, decision scenarios_must_fail_the_competitor_test).

## Body

Chronic: The re-prompting tax. Candidate B becomes the human sync layer across every AI tool they run — re-establishing context, copy-pasting between Claude Code, Cursor, and ChatGPT, maintaining a growing pile of markdown files or a Notion database they already suspect is a dead end (see the incumbent research_finding from this run, ent_9e105035543fed11658a3fcb). Cost is diffuse: attention, repetition, low-grade frustration, not a single event (primary_icp.md, Pain triggers). It is corroborated operationally by two distinct evaluator complaints that are chronic in character because they compound with sustained use rather than triggering once: (1) opacity — an evaluator (feedback [evaluator-record]) used Neotoma for ~1 month and 'has no sense of whether it is actually benefiting her'; an evaluator ([evaluator-record]) reports 'no visibility into when memories are being read' — both are a slow-burn trust erosion, not a single failure; (2) token cost — an evaluator measured the Neotoma MCP server at 19% of his Claude Code token usage ([evaluator-record]) and an evaluator independently reports 'Neotoma tool calls definitely chews through tokens' alongside otherwise-positive usage ([evaluator-record]) — both are cited in the register as a RECURRING OPERATE-TIME TAX, structurally proportional to usage (decision token_cost_is_a_standalone_decision), which is chronic by construction: it is invisible at install and only shows up after sustained use.

Acute: The crisis that converts. An agent acts confidently on wrong, stale, or lossy-compressed state, and the reader discovers the damage downstream — a reverted decision built on it, a nuanced choice flattened and silently overwritten, contradictory observations overwriting each other with no trace (primary_icp.md, Pain triggers; qualifier Q11, 'strongest single qualifier — a concrete loss event creates urgency'). This is a discrete, nameable event with a discoverable cost, not a mood. The register also surfaces a second acute shape worth carrying alongside the classic one: a chicken-and-egg 'light-up' moment where the acute trigger is not a state failure the reader already had, but the sudden realization — in conversation — that a recurring task they assumed was undelegatable is now delegable with a reliable state foundation underneath it (feedback ent_c15d5afc61ac03d3293e7a29). That is a second, distinct converting event for a LATENT-demand segment of Candidate B who has not yet attempted delegation and so has not yet felt the classic acute crisis; it does not replace the classic acute crisis for the ACTIVE-demand segment who already has.

Leads: The acute crisis leads. This is operator-decided, not re-derived: plan decision scenarios_must_fail_the_competitor_test (2026-08-21) explicitly overturned an earlier audit recommendation to promote the three 'tax' personas (context janitor, log archaeologist, inference babysitter) verbatim, on the finding that the original tax-led scenario set read as a standard retrieval-memory pitch and occupied the leftmost, most-read position — exactly the framing a competitor (mem0, Zep, any retrieval vendor) could equally claim. The register's own operative rule states it plainly: 'the chronic tax is what the ICP tolerates daily. The acute crisis is what converts them' (primary_icp.md); a reader who recognizes a tax they have already decided to absorb has been given no reason to act today. Rendered pages executed against this plan already apply the lead call — the shipped Neotoma hero, 'Your agents act confidently on state you already fixed,' was chosen specifically because it is the ACUTE crisis, and ruled out two chronic-tax candidate headlines (plan ent_98ef9d45f8a6896fed408f8f, todo pages-v2-vision-no-phases). This artifact makes that same lead call explicit and durable for future surfaces rather than leaving it implicit in one page's history.

## Gaps

CLOSED 2026-09-21: this run read ent_e1d1c7fb9c9b54e310c9cf4c directly (the full 167-entity corpus audit) rather than by citation, resolving the frequency question this gap previously flagged as unanswered. Of its 11 named operate-time entities, only 2 are instances of the classic acute crisis as this artifact defines it (an agent acting confidently on wrong/stale state, discovered downstream as a concrete loss): an evaluator ([evaluator-record] / [evaluator-record] — rated install 5/5, then hit a reducer that "silently overwrites a trusted correction in the active snapshot") and an evaluator deployment ([evaluator-record] — a production pipeline read stale state and acted on it: "TM Bounty #14 still shows pending_payment when it was actually paid"). The remaining 9 are chronic-shaped by the audit's own classification: token cost (2: an evaluator 19% of usage [evaluator-record], an evaluator [evaluator-record]), read-side opacity (2: an evaluator [evaluator-record] at ~1 month of use, an evaluator an evaluator [evaluator-record]), upgrade/maintenance mechanics (2), post-install disengagement to zero (1, not a crisis at all — habit failure), and query ergonomics (1). So within the audited corpus, named evaluators describe the CHRONIC pain roughly 4-5x as often as the classic acute one, and the chronic complaints are the ones evaluators volunteer unprompted in their own words ("chews through tokens," "no sense of whether it is benefiting her," "no visibility into when memories are being read") — the acute crisis, while real and sharply evidenced where it appears, is the rarer named event in this corpus, not the more frequent one. This does not overturn the lead call (see confidence field), because frequency-in-corpus is not the same test as convertibility, and the corpus itself is adoption-stage evaluator feedback rather than a controlled test of which framing converts faster — the operator's 2026-08-21 ruling (scenarios_must_fail_the_competitor_test) was about which SCENARIO framing a retrieval-memory competitor could not also claim, not about which pain is more frequently felt, and the acute crisis remains the one no competitor can claim regardless of its lower frequency. But the frequency asymmetry is real, cuts against the strength of the lead, and should inform how much weight any future surface puts on the acute crisis alone versus surfacing the chronic-opacity pain prominently (as ent_d82044c2475233e413a6dff0 already does via its fourth "You cannot tell if it is helping" card, added 2026-09-21, which this finding retroactively corroborates rather than contradicts). Separately: the 'light-up' chicken-and-egg acute shape (ent_c15d5afc61ac03d3293e7a29) remains single-session-sourced and thinly evidenced; this run found no additional corroboration for it in the corpus audit.
